subject: Website
bodyText:
Hi Tom
I have looked at the website for L S Lowry and am impressed with the prints for sale section. 
I think we should also offer Charlie’s prints with two options. A similar contemporary black frame or alternatively a single print delivered in a tube. Illustrated in a similar way with single picture and living room scenes to give buyers an idea of how the new painting would look in their home. 
I am wondering if glazed items should only be made available from my gallery ? Otherwise I think we would get many returns. 

I propose these words for the introduction to the print section.

I  will send you a selection of the prints to be offered for sale  together with an accompanying  description/story. 
Prices will be confirmed later. 

The first titled  The Men on the Seats is owned by Michael. 

We will need to set up a secure payment system. 
Sent from my iPhone

subject: Prints for sale on Website
bodyText:
PRINTS
FINE ART PRINTS
Explore our collection of Charlie Rogers fine art prints. Choose from a selection of Charlie’s most popular works, ranging from scenes of everyday life in the north of England to the bustling streets of Paris. 

Charlie’s life story is unsurpassed and is told perfectly in these precious moments in time. 

Each piece captures the unique style and depth that defines Charlie’s work, offering art lovers and collectors the chance to own a piece of recently discovered British art history.

The collection includes high-quality digital reproductions of Charlie’s paintings and drawings, each print offering something special and unique.

Explore the evocative imagery of Charlie  Rogers and bring the timeless appeal of his art into your home. 

You are invited to view our collection. 

Standard introduction for each print…

Discover the ‘Unknown Collection’ of Charlie Rogers. Create your own personal art collection with the addition of this scene depicting everyday life in the north of England during the second half of the twentieth

subject: Website print for sale
bodyText:
Hi Tom 
Here is the first of the paintings to be made available to purchase on the new website. 

The Men on the Seats, 1973

DESCRIPTION

This scene created in oil would have captured Charlie’s compulsion to record scenes of human interaction. It is highly probable the location was the sheltered seating area opposite the bandstand at Saltwell Park in Gateshead. Charlie visited the park regularly. Most of his early artwork were in oils before he was forced to stop and turn to painting with watercolours due to health concerns. 

A GOOD CHOICE ?

Yes, this is a perfect choice for those with the ambition to create their own Charlie Rogers Collection for their home. What an excellent conversation starter for visiting guests !

Dimensions 

All images are for illustrative purposes only

attachments.name: image00001.jpg
attachments.visualDescription: Photograph of an unframed oil painting resting against a pale grey wall, with masking tape and paper scraps visible along the top edge of the board. The picture shows a row of eight men in flat caps, suits and waistcoats seated along a green park bench, one man standing at the far right with a hand on his hip, and a small black dog trotting across the pale blue grey foreground. Palette is dominated by greys and slate blues with strong pink, orange and red accents in the waistcoats and background wall. Signed lower right, GHRogers.

subject: Print for sale
bodyText:
‘The Joke Shop, Gateshead-on-Tyne.’
1966  Watercolour and pen.

Description 
Your Charlie Rogers Collection will not be complete without a scene of the Railway Quarter.
The Railway Quarter is situated close to both the High Level and Tyne Bridge. It once boasted two railway stations - Gateshead East and Gateshead West. 
The area provided a wealth of  painting opportunities, including some of the region’s most iconic public houses, and of course the never-to-be-forgotten Joke Shop.

Charlie could always paint here, even in poor weather conditions, as shelter was provided by a large railway arch which features in many of his paintings. 

“Look at his paintings and you see scenes that you remember- that Gateshead joke shop by the High Level Bridge, gone but not forgotten.”

A GOOD CHOICE ?

Yes, this is a must-have scene to add to your Charlie Rogers Collection. An excellent conversation starter particularly for those interested in the heritage of Tyneside. 

Dimensions  TBC

All images are for illustrative purposes only. 

Sent from my iPhone

attachments.name: Paul Wright.jpg
attachments.visualDescription: The filename is misleading: this is not a photograph of a person. It is a small reproduction of the painting itself, a snow covered back lane between brick terraced houses, back yard walls and doors picked out in green, blue, red and purple, with a tall church tower and spire in the centre distance and two small figures with a dog walking away up the lane. Cool greys and whites with warm brick reds; oil handling. Signed and dated lower left, GHRogers 1980. This is the image used on the cover of Pursued by Bulldozers.

subject: Website Print for sale
bodyText:
Town Moor, Newcastle-upon-Tyne 1966
Based on the original watercolour.

Rogers was the Cezanne of Tyneside, painting the street scenes all around him. Some of his paintings were very gloomy as he was painting the decline of industries and recording social change. Others were more uplifting, the Hoppings at the Town Moor. 

In this painting Charlie has captured a typical day at the Hoppings,Europe's largest travelling funfair held annually at Newcastle Town Moor.

A Good Choice ?
Especially for those interested in the heritage of Northern England. 

Dimensions 

All images are for illustrative purposes only

attachments.name: Image.jpeg
attachments.visualDescription: Oil painting, photographed square on and cropped close to the picture edge. A brick terrace frontage with four adjoining front doors, cream, green, dark red and pale grey, each under a glazed fanlight and framed by white painted brick quoins, with stone steps down to the pavement. The green door stands ajar on a dark interior with a striped rug. Sash windows above, one with a blue plant pot on the sill. Muted plum and russet brickwork against cool grey stone. A faint signature and date sit in the bottom left corner.

attachments.name: Image.jpeg
attachments.visualDescription: Snow scene looking down a sloping shopping street, painted in washy watercolour and pen over pale board, though Brian labels the original oil on paper. A tall gable on the left carries a hand lettered sign reading CHRIST JESUS CAME INTO THE WORLD TO SAVE SINNERS, with shopfronts below and a BINGO sign and a CASTLE sign further down the hill. A woman in a long blue coat pushes a pram through deep snow with a child and a small dog beside her, and a man in a cap leans against a shop corner in the foreground. A dark stormy blue grey sky with chimney smoke fills the upper right. Signed lower left with the date 1970 and inscribed Bensham Road, Gateshead.

subject: Print for sale on Website
bodyText:
‘POT PIE BOB’S’ WELLINGTON STREET, GATESHEAD. 1977
Watercolour 

DESCRIPTION 
Charlie Rogers painted many cafe scenes during his many visits to Paris. However occasionally he was inspired to paint a cafe closer to home.
Charlie was a regular visitor to this cafe located near the High Level Bridge. 
The cafe was immortalised in the song  Fog on the Tyne written by Lindisfarne song writer Alan Hull.

“Sittin' in a sleazy snack bar sucking,
Sickly sausage rolls.
Slippin' down slowly, slippin' down sideways,
Think I'll sign off the dole.”
FOG ON THE TYNE

A GOOD CHOICE ??
Enough has been said already to convince anyone to own a replica of this delightful scene. 

Dimensions 
Original painting - 22 x 21cm
Mounted print- 30 x 25cm

Price - TBC

All images are for illustrative purposes only

attachments.name: IMG_3569.jpeg
attachments.visualDescription: Watercolour and pen study of a cafe shopfront set inside a dressed stone railway arch. The frontage is painted mid blue, with a white fascia lettered HIGH LEVEL CAFE, flanked by SANDWICHES TO CARRY OUT on the left and OUR MOTTO QUICK SERVICE on the right, and a Snack Bar sign in the right hand window. Red and white gingham half curtains hang in both windows and a pale wooden gate stands across the central doorway. A red pillar box and a yellow sign on a post sit to the right, on a loosely drawn flagstone pavement. Muted stone greys and ochres against the blue joinery. Signed lower left, GHRogers 1977, and inscribed POT-PIE BOB'S WELLINGTON ST. GATESHEAD.
